references.text: Proverbs describes a generation that is clean in its own eyes, yet has not been washed clean from its uncleanness. This reflects the attitude of those who trust in themselves and consider themselves righteous, as warned against in Proverbs 30:12.
Isaiah refers to those who say, 'Keep away, do not come near me, for I am too holy for you!' – a self-righteous attitude that despises others, similar to those Jesus addresses in Isaiah 65:5.
'Do you see someone who is wise in their own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for them.' This warning in Proverbs 26:12 targets the same self-righteous attitude that Jesus confronts.
The lawyer, seeking to justify himself, asked, 'Who is my neighbor?' This example in Luke 10:29 illustrates the same tendency toward self-righteousness that Jesus confronts.

Jesus said to the Pharisees, 'You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts.' Luke 16:15 directly addresses the self-righteous attitude that the parable in Luke 18:9 targets.
The Pharisees and scribes grumbled because Jesus welcomed sinners, revealing their contempt for others – the same attitude described in Luke 15:2-3 and addressed by Jesus through his parable.
Paul describes those who did not know God's righteousness and sought to establish their own, as stated in Romans 10:3. This is at the heart of the self-righteous attitude that Jesus warns against.
Paul asks, 'Why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise your brother?' Romans 14:10 warns against the contempt for others that characterized those Jesus spoke to.

Paul mentions his former life in which he trusted in the flesh and relied on his own righteousness under the law, as recorded in Philippians 3:4-6, illustrating the same self-confidence that Jesus confronts.

The church in Laodicea said, 'I am rich, I have prospered, and I need nothing,' without realizing their true condition. Revelation 3:17 reveals the same spiritual blindness that self-righteousness produces.

The Pharisee Simon despised the sinful woman and questioned Jesus because he allowed her to touch him. Luke 7:39 illustrates the contempt for others that characterizes those Jesus addresses in this parable.
